debate_title: Compute governance as a lever for AI safety: export contr...

conflicts.point: Whether capability-indexed tiered oversight using cryptographic model-weight logging can effectively govern distributed AI development without creating prohibitive compliance moats.

positions.stance: Dynamic capability thresholds tied to verifiable model weights and cryptographic logging can enforce oversight on frontier models while minimizing administrative friction for smaller developers.
Regulatory oversight mechanisms inevitably function as compliance moats that burden open-weight distribution and smaller innovators while failing to stop decentralized scaling.

verdicts.conflict: Whether capability-indexed tiered oversight using cryptographic model-weight logging can effectively govern distributed AI development without creating prohibitive compliance moats.
verdicts.rationale: Both sides offer sound theoretical models but lack empirical deployment data at scale. The safetyist side details audit mechanisms like electrical monitoring, while the skeptic side demonstrates real evasion vectors through multi-tenant colocation facilities.
